title: A Price Written on Two Tags
fact_notes: オリジナル教材。架空の例を用いた論説であり、実在の調査・史料・制度・実証結果ではない。制作台帳は来歴確認用。

sentences.en: A school shop offers notebooks in two different sizes.
sentences.ja: 学校の売店は二種類の大きさのノートを提供する。

sentences.en: The larger notebook costs more than the smaller one, although it also contains more pages.
sentences.ja: 大きいノートは小さいものより高いがページも多い。

sentences.en: A student compares the two prices and immediately decides that the smaller notebook is the cheaper choice.
sentences.ja: 生徒は二価格を比較しすぐ小さい方が安い選択だと決める。

sentences.en: His friend asks whether he intends to compare the cost of each notebook or the cost of an equal amount of writing space.
sentences.ja: 友人は各ノートの費用と同じ量の筆記空間の費用のどちらを比較するつもりか尋ねる。

sentences.en: The students discover that different ways of comparing prices can produce different conclusions.
sentences.ja: 価格比較の異なる方法は異なる結論を生み得ると生徒は気づく。

sentences.en: The smaller notebook requires less money at the moment of purchase.
sentences.ja: 小ノートは購入時により少ない金額しか必要としない。

sentences.en: However, the larger notebook might offer a lower price per page, depending on its price and number of pages.
sentences.ja: しかし価格とページ数次第では大きいノートの方が一ページ当たり安いかもしれない。

sentences.en: Neither measure alone establishes which notebook is more useful for every customer.
sentences.ja: どちらの尺度だけでも全顧客にどちらがより有用かは確定しない。

sentences.en: Some customers may need only a few pages for a short project.
sentences.ja: 短い活動に数ページしか必要としない客もいるかもしれない。

sentences.en: Others may use notebooks regularly and need a substantial amount of writing space over several months.
sentences.ja: 定期的にノートを使い数か月にわたりかなりの筆記空間を必要とする客もいるかもしれない。

sentences.en: The larger product may be economical for the second group without being the best choice for the first.
sentences.ja: 大きい製品は第二集団には経済的でも第一には最善でないかもしれない。

sentences.en: The students recognize that useful comparisons require attention to the purpose of a purchase.
sentences.ja: 有用な比較には購入目的への注意が必要と生徒は認識する。

sentences.en: For a classroom activity, they prepare a simple display explaining both the total price and the price per page.
sentences.ja: 教室活動として総価格と一ページ当たり価格を説明する簡単な展示を作る。

sentences.en: They also include information about the number of pages in each product.
sentences.ja: 各製品のページ数も情報に含める。

sentences.en: The intention is not to encourage every reader to choose the same notebook.
sentences.ja: 意図は全読者に同じノートを選ばせることではない。

sentences.en: Instead, the display helps readers decide which comparison is relevant to their own circumstances.
sentences.ja: 代わりに展示は自分の事情にどの比較が関連するか判断を助ける。

sentences.en: A price is an important source of information, but its meaning depends on what is being compared.
sentences.ja: 価格は重要な情報源だがその意味は何を比較するかに依存する。

sentences.en: A smaller total cost and a smaller cost per unit are not always the same thing.
sentences.ja: より小さい総費用とより小さい単位費用は常に同じではない。

sentences.en: Knowing the difference allows customers to ask more useful questions before buying a product.
sentences.ja: 違いを知ると購入前により有用な問いを問える。

sentences.en: The two price tags become an invitation to think about value rather than merely looking for the smallest number.
sentences.ja: 二つの値札は単に最小の数を見るのでなく価値について考える誘いになる。

vocabulary.definition: measurements of how large things are
act of obtaining goods for money
give someone a reason to act

questions.prompt: What product does the shop sell?
What does the friend's question introduce?
options: A new way to draw pictures.
A requirement to buy both products.
Two possible ways of comparing cost.
A plan to stop selling notebooks.

questions.prompt: Which notebook needs less money at purchase?
Why might the larger notebook be economical?
options: It necessarily costs less in total.
Its price per page could be lower.

questions.prompt: What might a customer need for a short project?
options: A larger notebook in every case.

questions.prompt: Why may the best choice differ among customers?
options: The two notebooks have identical features.
Every customer values only total page count.
Their intended use and need for pages differ.

questions.prompt: What information is shown on the display?
options: Total price, price per page and number of pages.
questions.explanation_ja: 総額・単価・ページ数。

questions.prompt: What is the intention of the display?
options: Make everyone choose the larger notebook.
Help readers select a comparison relevant to their needs.
Understanding value requires choosing a price comparison relevant to the purchase.
The product with the smallest total price is always best.
A large number of pages always means a worse purchase.
questions.explanation_ja: 購入目的に応じた価格比較。

grammar.focus: although it also contains more pages

paraphrases.source: The larger notebook costs more than the smaller one, although it also contains more pages.
paraphrases.rewrite: The larger notebook is more expensive but has more pages.

paraphrases.source: Neither measure alone establishes which notebook is more useful for every customer.
paraphrases.rewrite: No single one of these measures identifies the best product for everyone.

paraphrases.source: The larger product may be economical for the second group without being the best choice for the first.
paraphrases.rewrite: The larger notebook can save money for frequent users but not necessarily for short projects.

paraphrases.source: Knowing the difference allows customers to ask more useful questions before buying a product.
paraphrases.rewrite: Understanding the distinction helps customers ask better questions.

discourse.role_ja: 一律の選択でなく情報提供。

cloze.explanation_ja: 自分の事情に関連する。
